scene.title: The Car Sale: One Action, Multiple Consequences
scene.description: Mark and Sarah owe their mutual friend Florence €5,000. Mark offers Sarah's red Austin Mini to Florence to settle the debt. Sarah does not agree to sell it.
scene.action: Mark offers Sarah's car to Florence to settle a €5,000 debt.
scene.time: Tomorrow, 10:00 a.m. (a scenario label, not a calendar date)
context: Mark and Sarah owe their mutual friend Florence €5,000.
Sarah owns a red Austin Mini.
Mark offers the car to Florence to settle the debt.
Sarah does not agree to sell it.
Whether Florence knew of Sarah's objection beforehand is unknown.
Whether Mark has authority to sell the car is unknown.
The scene ends before the handover is completed.

actors.name: Mark
unknown: Whether he has authority to sell the car

inferences.text: May feel pressure to resolve the debt, or defensive once Sarah objects.
May defend the plan or back down.

actors.name: Sarah
preferences: Does not agree to sell her car
unknown: Whether she would accept an alternative
How attached she is to the car

inferences.text: “A decision about my car is being made without me.”
May feel upset, worried or let down.
May refuse the sale outright or ask for another way to repay.

actors.name: Florence
unknown: Whether she knew of Sarah's objection before arriving
Whether she wants the car at all

inferences.text: “I want to be repaid, but not with a car that is in dispute.”
May delay the handover or suggest another repayment plan.

events.description: Mark stands beside Sarah's red Mini, holding its keys. Florence waits near the garage entrance. Sarah stands beside the car.
Mark offers the Mini to Florence to settle the debt.
events.dialogue: Florence, we owe you €5,000. I'm offering you the Mini to settle the debt.

events.description: Mark extends the keys toward Florence.
events.animation: extend right arm, keys in hand

events.description: Sarah objects to the sale.
events.dialogue: Stop. That's my car, and I don't agree to sell it.

events.description: Florence pauses.
Florence asks whether Sarah agreed.
events.dialogue: Mark, did Sarah agree to this?

events.description: Mark lowers his hand. The keys remain with him.

unknowns: Whether Mark has authority to sell the car.
Whether Florence knew of Sarah's objection before arriving.
caveats: The sale is proposed and disputed. Ownership has not transferred and the debt is not settled.
The dialogue is illustrative demo content, not a recording or a model prediction.

conflicts.description: Mark's goal (settle the debt with the car) conflicts with Sarah's stated position (she does not agree to sell it).
Florence's repayment now depends on a transaction that is disputed.

consequences.description: His proposed repayment plan is challenged by Sarah's objection.
His relationship with Sarah may be affected.
questions: How do Mark and Sarah usually settle disagreements?

consequences.description: Sarah objects: her car is offered without her agreement.
Florence must decide how to respond to the dispute.
The €5,000 debt remains unpaid at the end of the scene.
The car and keys remain in the garage during the depicted scene; the keys stay with Mark.
The disagreement could affect the friendship between the three.
Vehicle registration may become relevant if a valid sale is eventually agreed.
assumptions: A valid sale is agreed later.
questions: Does Mark have authority to sell the car?

consequences.description: Everyone present sees the keys held out and hears Sarah's objection; Florence asks about consent right after hearing it.
No record changes during the scene: no payment is made and no registration transfer is started.
No specific societal impact is established.
No national economic impact is established.
No specific global, environmental or ecosystem impact is established.

assumptions: Florence is willing to wait for part of the money.
branches.summary: Mark withdraws the offer and the three discuss paying Florence in instalments.

Mark accepts Sarah's objection.
events.dialogue: You're right. I should have discussed this with you first.

events.description: Sarah steps away from the car.
Sarah wants another way to repay.
events.dialogue: We still need to repay Florence. Let's find another way.

events.description: Florence offers to wait for part of it.
events.dialogue: I can wait for part of it if we agree on a payment plan.

events.description: Mark picks up a notebook from the workbench.

goal_changes.change: His plan changes from selling the car to a repayment plan; settling the debt is still possible.
Keeps the decision about her car.
May be repaid over time rather than at once.

layers.name: Action or event
layers.examines: Who acts, why, their goal and desired outcome, and what happens
layers.osi_role: A networking application creates or receives information
layers.engine: The scene script (acm.scene): actors, goals, ordered events and their state changes; single sentences are parsed by MLM's phrase model

layers.name: Physical world
layers.examines: Objects, materials, movement, forces, location and energy
layers.osi_role: Transmits raw bits as signals over a physical medium
layers.engine: Scene state tracks positions, holders and owners (2D player). Forces and materials: a 2D matter.js stand-in in the Image/Video chat; a 3D physics engine (Unreal Engine 5, Chaos) is planned

layers.name: Perception and observation
layers.examines: Images, video, audio, speech, sensors and observations
layers.osi_role: Transfers frames across a local network link
layers.engine: Scene observations and who can see or hear each event. Image/video recognition in the Image/Video chat uses replayed detections; a vision-language model and detector are planned

layers.name: Consequence routing
layers.examines: Determines which world models, actors and systems should examine an event
layers.osi_role: Addresses and routes packets across networks (routing)
layers.engine: acm.scene.layers.route: explicit rules over each event's verb, type, objects and effects, plus the events each consequence cites as evidence

layers.name: Human and social
layers.examines: Goals, behaviour, dialogue, relationships and group reactions
layers.osi_role: Provides end-to-end data transport between applications
layers.engine: The script model (goals, stated positions, possible feelings, conflicts) and next scenes from the authored demo or the local next-action model

layers.name: Digital and information systems
layers.examines: Applications, records, calculations, permissions and workflows
layers.osi_role: Establishes, manages and ends communication sessions
layers.engine: Explicit state changes and calculations (rule engine: has(x, y), amounts). No external system (registry, bank) is connected

layers.name: Business and institutions
layers.examines: Organisations, operations, processes, finance and policies
layers.osi_role: Represents or transforms data, including formats and encoding
layers.engine: Obligations in the scene (debts, agreements) and the rule engine's organisation-scoped impact rules

layers.name: Society and collective systems
layers.examines: Economy, markets, society, public governance and politics
layers.osi_role: Provides network services used by applications, such as web and email
layers.engine: The rule engine's society- and country-scoped impact rules. No economic or political model yet

layers.name: Planetary and ecosystem
layers.osi_role: (no OSI layer: the outermost system every other one depends on)
layers.engine: The rule engine's earth-scoped impact rules (e.g. flying and emissions). No ecosystem model yet
